{
  "summary": "Deprecates the `encryptwallet` RPC command, which encrypts an existing unencrypted wallet. Adjusts several functional tests to create wallets encrypted from inception rather than encrypting them after creation, gating tests that specifically test `encryptwallet` behind the deprecation flag.",
  "problem": "Encrypting a wallet after it has already been created unencrypted is unsafe and creates maintenance overhead. Unencrypted key material can linger on disk, encryption regenerates keys so older backups can lead to fund loss, and encrypting wallets with imported descriptors can change spending conditions unexpectedly.",
  "evidence": [
    "PR description points to issue #26607: 'Encrypting a wallet that has manually imported descriptors will cause the wallet to change the spending conditions out from under the user.'",
    "PR description highlights data security risks: 'No efforts are made to ensure that remnants of unencrypted key material are not left on the user's disk... and for some SSD's infeasible.'",
    "PR description highlights backup risk: 'Because new keys are made after encryption, restoring from a backup made before encryption may result in loss of funds.'",
    "RFC issue #36027 ('[rfc] Remove encrypting wallets that already exist') tracks discussion on phasing out this functionality."
  ],
  "dependencies": {
    "depends_on": [],

  "changed_since_previous": "",
  "card": "Deprecates the encryptwallet RPC for encrypting wallets that were created unencrypted, preparing it for eventual removal. Post-creation encryption poses security and fund-loss risks: plaintext keys may persist on storage, newly generated keys invalidate previous backups, and wallets with imported descriptors can have their spending conditions altered (issue #26607). result.summary: Deprecates the `encryptwallet` RPC command, which encrypts an existing unencrypted wallet. Adjusts several functional tests to create wallets encrypted from inception rather than encrypting them after creation, gating tests that specifically test `encryptwallet` behind the deprecation flag.
result.problem: Encrypting a wallet after it has already been created unencrypted is unsafe and creates maintenance overhead. Unencrypted key material can linger on disk, encryption regenerates keys so older backups can lead to fund loss, and encrypting wallets with imported descriptors can change spending conditions unexpectedly.
evidence: PR description points to issue #26607: 'Encrypting a wallet that has manually imported descriptors will cause the wallet to change the spending conditions out from under the user.'
PR description highlights data security risks: 'No efforts are made to ensure that remnants of unencrypted key material are not left on the user's disk... and for some SSD's infeasible.'
PR description highlights backup risk: 'Because new keys are made after encryption, restoring from a backup made before encryption may result in loss of funds.'
RFC issue #36027 ('[rfc] Remove encrypting wallets that already exist') tracks discussion on phasing out this functionality.
result.scope_notes: The diff mainly consists of functional test refactoring to avoid calling `encryptwallet` across multiple test suites.
result.card: Deprecates the encryptwallet RPC for encrypting wallets that were created unencrypted, preparing it for eventual removal. Post-creation encryption poses security and fund-loss risks: plaintext keys may persist on storage, newly generated keys invalidate previous backups, and wallets with imported descriptors can have their spending conditions altered (issue #26607). Creating encrypted wallets at creation time remains supported. Several functional tests are refactored to set up encrypted wallets at creation rather than encrypting existing ones.

risk.why: Deprecating an RPC command can break external scripts or user workflows that rely on encrypting wallets after creation.
